subject.title: fix(tts-local-cli): cap local CLI speech outputs

question: Should tts-local-cli ship fixed 50 MiB audio and 1 MiB stderr caps as non-configurable provider policy, or should this PR align the limit with an existing/shared media cap before merge?
rationale: Current docs do not define a local CLI output-size limit, and this PR intentionally changes oversized outputs from successful results into deterministic errors; automation cannot choose that compatibility policy for maintainers.

options.title: Accept Fixed Caps After Proof
options.body: Merge once the contributor adds real local CLI TTS proof and maintainers accept oversized-output failures as the safety tradeoff.

options.title: Align With Shared Media Limits
options.body: Ask the PR to reuse an existing media limit or documented cap source before merge so local CLI behavior stays aligned with other speech providers.

options.title: Pause For Configurable Cap Design
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want very large local CLI outputs to remain supported through an explicit configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Accept Fixed Caps After Proof
recommendation.body: Merge once the contributor adds real local CLI TTS proof and maintainers accept oversized-output failures as the safety tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced and recently maintained the provider and adjacent TTS surfaces on current main.
